text: Harbour City led 2-0 at halftime, leveraging their patient short-passing 4-2-3-1 formation to build methodical attacks, including a 17-pass sequence for Elias Okafor's opener and a set-piece goal by Marek Barros [#905] [#975]. Marek Barros was influential with 1 goal, 2 assists, and 9 interceptions but could not prevent the collapse after Joon Whitfield's red card at 43', which likely weakened Harbour City's defensive resilience [#870, #871, player_of_the_match]. Seabrook Town’s tactical adjustment at 65', increasing press intensity, directness, and line height, successfully disrupted Harbour City's rhythm, enabling faster direct counter-attacks highlighted by Kian Romano’s decisive goals in added time [#1361] [#1882] [#1906]. Despite trailing 2-0, Seabrook Town's exploitation of transitional moments through wide, crossing play in a 3-4-3 formation turned the match, showcasing effective adaptation under pressure [#1448]. The key coaching point is to prepare for tactical shifts by maintaining defensive organization after red cards, ensuring quick in-game adjustments to counter increased pressing and direct attacks.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for coach audience in en

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals with a combined xG of 2.044, showing efficient finishing and strong attacking performance [#1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].
- Harbour City led 2-0 at halftime with goals from Elias Okafor (xG 0.111) and Marek Barros (xG 0.009) but conceded 4 unanswered in the second half [#905, #975].
- Seabrook Town had greater overall possession at 53.4% compared to Harbour City's 46.6%, assisting their comeback [team_stats].
- Marek Barros was named Player of the Match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 5 key passes, 9 interceptions, and a 9.8 rating despite his team losing [player_of_the_match].
- A red card to Joon Whitfield at 43' likely impacted Harbour City's defensive capacity before the comeback goals by Seabrook Town [#870, #871].

- Seabrook Town's late goals came after regaining possession and executing quick, direct counter-attacks. For example, Kian Romano’s 90+2' goal arose from a regain and a fast two-pass combination with Aiden Quinlan, showing effective exploitation of transitional moments in a 3-4-3 formation emphasizing wide and crossing play [#1882].
- Harbour City’s initial goals reflected their patient short-passing style within a 4-2-3-1 setup: their first goal at 45’ was the product of a 17-pass build-up over 56.7 seconds starting from open play, demonstrating controlled possession and methodical buildup culminating in a through ball assist from Marek Barros to Elias Okafor [#905].
- The second goal for Harbour City at 47’ came from a corner (set piece), with Barros scoring off a cross, indicative of using set pieces to exploit defensive weaknesses; this also shows Barros's tactical influence as creator and scorer under a formation favoring structured attacking patterns [#975].
- Seabrook Town’s tactical shift around the 65’ mark to press higher and increase directness and line height (from press 0.66 to 0.84, directness 0.42 to 0.57, line height 0.6 to 0.72) reflected an intent to disrupt Harbour City’s patient style, pushing more aggressively to regain ball and execute quicker attacks, which led to their equalizer at 69’ after a regain and brief passing sequence [#1361, #1448].
